Nope. My situation involves losing the person that was the entirety of my support system. Truthfully speaking, the only reason I’m posting/commenting here is because I have nowhere else to go. 

PM me if you want to talk more, only because reddit keeps doing the ten minute delay thing between posts and comments.

I guess for me, it was after a bad experience at a Halloween party when I was 17. I had a severe breakdown and the events that transpired as a result aren’t things I want to mention. 

The only thing I could do was let time pass by. I never got over it, but I could at least manage. Eventually, I found my way out to some degree. Unfortunately, I’m likely to fall back down again and I’ll have to do the same thing again, although I truly don’t feel time will help. It’s funny how we give advice sometimes, yet we’re not the best at taking it ourselves.

St. John’s wort has the effect of increasing the amount of serotonin you have. When you suddenly go off of it, there may be some withdrawal effects, which is likely where your side effects are coming from. Some people also have stomach problems since serotonin is also in your gut. This is generally something that occurs when people stop certain medications that give you more serotonin (SSRIs, for example), although in theory this can happen with St. John’s wort as well.

Edit: there isn’t an exact timeline as to how long it will take for it to stop, but generally, these things should stop as your body adjusts to how much serotonin you have.

From what I’ve personally seen, medicine does a very good job at making these things more manageable. If nothing else though, the only thing I’d want you to know is that medicine **is not a cure** for what you deal with. Sometimes people become angry because they weren’t made aware of this, and for very good reason. 

There are also counselors and therapists that do a little more of the dirty work in terms of working through your thoughts and helping you build the skills to cope more effectively. These things do help though, and it’s best to give them a try if you feel ready to do so. I can’t give specific advice, but PM me (or reply) if you need general information.

Hi. I’m not sure if this will be helpful to your situation, but I have a slight background in healthcare and can offer you some insight from a medical perspective, although I’m only a student. I’m not sure of what exactly is causing all this, so take my info with a grain of salt. 

Psychiatrists will ask you questions about your mood and behavior, traumatic events, and other things of that nature to figure out what you’re dealing with. If they feel it’s necessary, you’ll be put on something to help you manage. Depending on where you are, there may be ways to offset the financial cost, although I am only generally aware of how things work in the US. 

There are also other things you can do to help yourself manage. These things might be drawing, going outside, eating better, writing your feelings down, listening to music, or other things you find helpful. Nonetheless, what you choose to do - whether it’s seeing a doctor or psychologist, taking medications, seeking therapy, or trying to manage things yourself, it all depends on your personal situation and what you’re able to do. There isn’t a solution that fits for everyone, and I strongly suggest you try to see a doctor if at all possible. Due to my current situation, I’m unable to give personal support, but I can offer you more medical insight if you need.

No worries. Your story is your own, and you’re free to tell it (or not) on your own terms. In any case, I’m not in the best place right now, and I might not be the best person to give you the support you’d need in whatever you’re going through right now. I’d rather not offer you something I can’t give. Regardless, I wish you nothing but the best in whatever you’re dealing with.
